name: Cenegenics
tagline: Physician-led age management with 20 US centers and openly published program pricing
description:
Cenegenics runs a physician-led age management program built around heavy up-front diagnostic testing. New members start with the Performance Health Assessment, which covers biomarker panels, VO2 max, DEXA body composition, CIMT, advanced coronary CT and cognitive testing. The onboarding blood draw is done by a phlebotomist who comes to your home or office. From there a physician and a dedicated health coach build an ongoing plan across nutrition, exercise, nutraceuticals and, where clinically indicated, hormone therapy.

Regenerative treatment is not offered at every center. The Jacksonville practice, led by Earl H. Eye, MD, FACCP, lists Wharton's jelly derived stem cells and exosomes alongside sexual health therapies. Miami lists PRP as a named service. In New York City, Joseph Bosiljevac, Jr. MD, PhD, FACS came out of cardiovascular surgery and regenerative medicine and brings those therapies into his longevity work. The other US centers stay with diagnostics, hormone optimization and lifestyle programming.

The company was founded in 1997 and is based in Las Vegas, with 20 US centers listed on its locations page and seven more abroad. Pricing is published rather than quoted privately. The initial assessment runs $4,495 to $13,000 depending on how much testing the physician orders, and Cenegenics puts the ongoing annual cost at $14,000 to $21,000 once the monthly program fee and supplement supply are counted. Insurance is not accepted, though FSA and HSA funds can be used, and no long-term contract is required.

priceNote: Cenegenics publishes its own pricing, which is unusual in this category. Per the company FAQ, the Performance Health Assessment runs $4,495 to $13,000 depending on how much testing the physician orders. After that the program fee is $550 to $750 a month, and nutraceuticals and medications are $350 to $600 a month, which Cenegenics totals at an average of $14,000 to $21,000 a year. Insurance is not accepted, though FSA and HSA funds can be used. Regenerative treatment prices are set per center.

team.name: Jeffrey Park Leake
team.title: Senior Institute Physician and Director of Education
team.bio: Based at the Las Vegas center and Director of Education for the Cenegenics Education and Research Foundation, the arm that trains physicians in the company's age management protocols. Cenegenics says he has trained more than 800 physicians and wrote the Textbook of Age Management Medicine.

team.name: Earl H. Eye
team.title: President and Chief Medical Officer, Cenegenics Jacksonville
team.bio: More than four decades of clinical experience and board certification across five specialties. Graduated magna cum laude from West Virginia University School of Medicine and completed his Internal Medicine residency at the University of Florida, with fellowships in infectious diseases, pulmonary diseases and critical care. He led a pulmonary and infectious disease practice from 1975 to 2008 and moved into preventive and age management medicine in 2004. He is the physician behind the Wharton's jelly stem cell and exosome offering in Jacksonville.

team.name: Joseph Bosiljevac, Jr.
team.title: Center Physician, Cenegenics New York City
team.bio: Trained originally as a cardiovascular surgeon, with a career spanning five decades. He earned a doctorate in natural medicine alongside his surgical training and built his regenerative practice treating retired NFL and NBA athletes, then military special operations personnel, before relocating to New York City to work in age management medicine.

team.name: Beth Traylor
team.title: Senior Institute Physician
team.bio: Past President of the Board of the Cenegenics Education and Research Foundation, with more than 40 years of clinical experience, based at the Las Vegas center.

team.name: Lloyd Camper
team.title: Center Physician, Atlanta and Miami
team.bio: Board certified in Family Medicine and Sports Medicine. Medical degree from USC, Family Medicine residency at the University of Miami and a Sports Medicine fellowship at Kaiser Permanente Fontana. Fluent in French and Spanish.

team.name: Bina Patel
team.title: Center Physician, Las Vegas
team.bio: Diplomate of the American Board of Internal Medicine, board certified in Integrative Medicine, and certified by the Institute for Functional Medicine.

team.name: Shahab Mokhtare
team.title: Center Physician, Las Vegas
team.bio: Board-trained Family Medicine physician at the Las Vegas center, with a focus on preventive care and performance optimization.

faqs.question: Does every Cenegenics center offer stem cell therapy?
faqs.answer: No. Regenerative treatment is location specific. Jacksonville lists Wharton's jelly derived stem cells and exosomes, Miami lists PRP, and the New York City physician folds regenerative therapies into his longevity practice. The remaining US centers focus on diagnostics, hormone optimization, nutrition and fitness. Ask the specific center before you assume it is available.

faqs.question: Are the cell and exosome therapies FDA approved?
faqs.answer: No. Cell and exosome therapies are investigational and are not approved by the FDA for anti-aging or the other uses offered here. They are elective procedures and are not a replacement for standard medical care.

faqs.question: What does the program cost?
faqs.answer: The Performance Health Assessment runs $4,495 to $13,000 depending on how much testing your physician orders. After that the monthly program fee is $550 to $750 and the nutraceutical and medication supply is $350 to $600 per month. Cenegenics puts the yearly average at $14,000 to $21,000.

faqs.question: Does Cenegenics take insurance, and is there a contract?
faqs.answer: Insurance is not accepted. Cenegenics describes itself as a private practice meant to supplement the care your primary care physician provides, and says FSA or HSA funds can be used to pay. On contracts, the company states there is no long-term commitment or contract required.

faqs.question: Is hormone therapy required?
faqs.answer: No. The company says hormone therapy is used only if clinically indicated and describes it as one of several available therapies rather than the centerpiece of the program.

faqs.question: Where is the head office and how do I reach them?
